Total.Recall v2.6.0-preview.1
Persistent memory server for AI agents doing .NET code coverage work.

Usage:
  total-recall                    Start MCP stdio server (intended for VS Code; reads JSON-RPC from stdin)
  total-recall init <repo-path>   Auto-discover repo layout, write config.json, print mcp.json snippet
  total-recall doctor [--ns <n>]  Health-check data root + namespace configs
  total-recall scan [options]     Run scanners and produce JSONL data
  total-recall report <sub>       Print telemetry reports (tool-stats, efficiency, scorecard, ...)
  total-recall --version          Print version and exit
  total-recall --help             Show this help

First 5 minutes:
  1. cd <your-repo>
  2. total-recall init .
  3. Paste the printed JSON block into .vscode/mcp.json
  4. Run the printed 'total-recall scan ...' command to populate data
  5. Restart VS Code and ask Copilot: "get testable targets, top 5"

Environment:
  TOTAL_RECALL_DATA          Root data directory (default: 'data')
  TOTAL_RECALL_NAMESPACE     Default namespace (default: 'default')
  TOTAL_RECALL_SOURCE_ROOT   Target repo source root (for get_source_snippet)
  TOTAL_RECALL_LOG_LEVEL     debug|info|warn|error|quiet (default: info)
  TOTAL_RECALL_MODE          off|passive|active-eval (default: passive)

Each sub-command supports --help for detailed options.

result.stdout:
Usage: total-recall init <repo-path> [options]

Auto-discovers the layout of a target .NET repo, writes config.json,
and prints a ready-to-paste .vscode/mcp.json block. Does NOT run the
scanner — run 'total-recall scan' (the printed command) afterwards.

Arguments:
  <repo-path>          Path to the target repo's root directory

Options:
  --namespace <name>   Namespace subdirectory (default: derived from repo dir name)
  --data-root <path>   Override data root (default: TOTAL_RECALL_DATA env var or 'data')
  --help, -h           Show this help

Examples:
  total-recall init C:\repos\MyProject
  total-recall init . --namespace myproject
  total-recall init ../OtherRepo --data-root C:\total-recall-data

result.stdout:
Total.Recall Scanner v2.6.0-preview.1

Usage: total-recall scan [options]

Options:
  --assembly <path>      Path to target .NET assembly (.dll) for type registry scan
  --coverage <path>      Path to Cobertura XML coverage report for coverage gaps
  --tests <path>         Path to test project directory for test inventory scan
  --source-root <path>   Path to target repo source root (enables get_source_snippet)
  --output <path>        Override data output directory
  --namespace <name>     Namespace subdirectory under TOTAL_RECALL_DATA root
  --enrich               Cross-reference coverage with type registry + test inventory
  --analyze              Run static analysis: dependency graph, coupling metrics, clusters
  --watch                Watch mode: re-scan automatically when files change (Ctrl+C to stop)
  --test-framework <fw>  Test framework: xunit (default), nunit, mstest
  --mock-library <lib>   Mock library: moq (default), nsubstitute, fakeiteasy
  --test-namespace-pattern <pat>  Namespace pattern for test classes (default: "{Namespace}.Tests")
                                  Use {Namespace} for full, {RootNamespace}/{Rest} for split
  --help, -h             Show this help

Examples:
  # Full scan with source root
  total-recall scan \
    --assembly "path/to/Server.dll" \
    --coverage "path/to/coverage.cobertura.xml" \
    --tests "path/to/UnitTest" \
    --source-root "path/to/Server/src" \
    --namespace myproject \
    --enrich --analyze

  # Full scan for an NUnit + NSubstitute project
  total-recall scan \
    --assembly "path/to/MyApp.dll" \
    --tests "path/to/MyApp.Tests" \
    --namespace myapp \
    --test-framework nunit \
    --mock-library nsubstitute \
    --enrich

  # Just re-parse coverage after a new test run
  total-recall scan --coverage "path/to/coverage.cobertura.xml" --namespace myproject --enrich

  # Watch mode: auto-rescan on file changes
  total-recall scan \
    --assembly "path/to/Server.dll" \
    --coverage "path/to/coverage.cobertura.xml" \
    --tests "path/to/UnitT

result.stdout:
Usage: total-recall report <sub-command> [options]

Sub-commands:
  tool-stats     Per-tool call counts, p50/p95 latency, response bytes
  efficiency     Session-level tokens / bytes / cycles / dedupe report
  scorecard      Per-model aggregated metrics across sessions+tasks+evals
  cycles         Recent detected behaviour cycles (re-query, context-loss, oscillation)
  sessions       Session history + plateau warning + lines-per-test ROI
  leaderboard    Per-model eval pass rate / avg score
  bugs           Class-scoped bug reports (latest record per id wins)

Options:
  --ns <name>        Namespace to query (default: TOTAL_RECALL_NAMESPACE env var)
  --last <N>         Limit results (cycles default 20, sessions default 5, bugs default 50)
  --pattern <name>   Filter cycles by pattern: re-query | context-loss | oscillation
  --class <name>     (bugs) Filter by class (partial match)
  --severity <s>     (bugs) Filter by severity: low|medium|high|critical
  --status <s>       (bugs) Filter by status: open|triaged|fixed|wontfix|all (default: open)
  --format <json|table>  Output format (default: json)

JSON output is suitable for piping through 'ConvertFrom-Json | Format-Table'
(PowerShell) or 'jq'. Use --format table for a built-in text table.

Examples:
  total-recall report tool-stats --ns myproject
  total-recall report cycles --pattern re-query --last 50
  total-recall report scorecard --format table
